query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive workflow that combines (1) ab-initio phonon spectra calculated on a small set of special-quasirandom structures with (2) machine-learned regression of configurationally averaged mass- and strain-fluctuation scattering rates will identify face-centred-cubic and body-centred-cubic high-entropy alloys (≥4 principal metallic elements, 5–35 at.% each) whose room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity κL is below 1.5 W m-1 K-1 with a mean absolute error < 0.25 W m-1 K-1—roughly a factor-of-two improvement over state-of-the-art virtual-crystal / Callaway estimates.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic or near-equiatomic FCC or BCC high-entropy alloys containing only metallic elements (no light interstitials), fully homogenised, polycrystalline, grain size >10 µm, measured at 300 K.
generation.intervention: Apply the proposed ab-initio-plus-ML workflow to predict κL for candidate HEAs before synthesis.
generation.conditions: Temperature 300 K; compositions restricted to 4–7 transition-metal elements with atomic-mass range 40–200 amu; single-phase solid solutions without second phases.
generation.structural_mediator: Configurational mass and strain disorder in the random solid solution, captured by the averaged phonon group velocities and scattering phase space output by the workflow.
generation.mechanism: The workflow explicitly samples the disorder-broadened phonon dispersion and couples it to machine-learned scattering models, thus capturing (i) enhanced point-defect scattering from large mass variance and (ii) strain-field scattering from atomic-size mismatch—both dominant pathways that suppress κL in HEAs and are not fully included in virtual-crystal approximations.
generation.predicted_outcome: For a test set of at least five previously unreported HEAs within the stated composition space, predicted κL values will differ from experimental time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) measurements by ≤ 0.25 W m-1 K-1 on average, and all predictions will correctly classify the alloys as κL < 1.5 W m-1 K-1.
generation.baseline: Conventional virtual-crystal or Callaway models using averaged masses and elastic constants, which show ~0.5 W m-1 K-1 mean absolute error and ~30 % false-classification rate for low-κ HEAs.
generation.boundary: Not expected to hold for (a) HEAs containing >3 at.% light interstitials (C, N, O), (b) strongly anharmonic ordered phases, (c) temperatures below magnetic ordering where magnon scattering dominates, or (d) nanocrystalline samples where boundary scattering is dominant.
generation.uncertainty: Limited published κL data for HEAs restricts statistical confidence; the degree to which a few SQS structures capture the full configurational space is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Select five new single-phase FCC or BCC HEAs that span a wide mass-variance range, predict their κL using the workflow, synthesise bulk ingots by arc-melting + homogenisation, verify single-phase character by XRD and SEM-EDS, and measure κL at 300 K via TDTR.
measurements: TDTR thermal conductivity at 300 K for each alloy
XRD lattice parameter for phase verification
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mean absolute error between predicted and measured κL exceeds 0.25 W m-1 K-1 OR any alloy predicted to have κL < 1.5 W m-1 K-1 is experimentally found to have κL ≥ 1.5 W m-1 K-1, the hypothesis is falsified.
